observation_summary: The PosixParser continues to process (burst) tokens even after encountering a non-option character when stopAtNonOption is enabled, leading to incorrect parsing results.
hypothesis: The parser's token bursting logic lacks a termination condition when stopAtNonOption is true and a non-option character is encountered, causing it to continue processing the remainder of the token incorrectly.
prediction: Adding a 'break' statement after the 'process(token.substring(i))' call within the 'else if (stopAtNonOption)' block will correctly halt the bursting process.
experiment_rationale: The provided fix diff shows exactly the insertion of a 'break' statement in the identified logic block, confirming that the issue was an incomplete iteration/processing strategy.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a procedural error in the token bursting algorithm. The parser failed to stop processing when it should have, which is a classic algorithmic control flow issue. It is not a missing guard (Checking) because the condition 'stopAtNonOption' was already being checked; the issue was the lack of a 'break' to terminate the loop/process, which is a procedural/algorithmic step correction.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The condition 'stopAtNonOption' was already correctly identified and entered; the failure was in the subsequent procedural action (the lack of a break to stop the loop).
